newsitem.title: USA: Tyler eyes expansion of auto parts unit.
newsitem.headline: Tyler eyes expansion of auto parts unit.

text.p: Tyler Corp said Friday that it weas reviewing the potential expansion opportunities for Forest City Auto Parts in markets where the unit has its greatest strengths.
The company said it was taking this step "in an effort to return sales back to acceptable levels."

It said that same-store sales at Forest City declined 10 percent and 11 percent during the second quarter and six months ended June 30, 1997, respectively, due to continued competitive pressures in its market areas.

"The effect of the shortfall in sales was mitigated by a slightly higher gross margin as well as a reduction in operating expenses of over $1.5 million during the first half of 1997," said Bruce Wilkinson, president and chief executive officer of the company.
Tyler also operates Institutional Financing Services, which provides products for fund-raising programs.

In the second quarter ended June 30, Tyler said it posted a net loss of $1.1 million, or $0.06 per share, compared with a similar net loss of $1.1 million, or $0.06 per share, for the corresponding quarter a year ago.

Consolidated net sales were $23.0 million for the 1997 second quarter compared with $26.6 million in the same period in 1996. Second-quarter 1997 sales contributed by Forest City and Institutional Financing were $20.5 million and $2.5 million, respectively.
